newsitem.title: POLAND: Zloty firms slightly after c.bank rate rise pledge.
newsitem.headline: Zloty firms slightly after c.bank rate rise pledge.

text.p: The Polish zloty strenghtened by 0.3 point against the currency basket after a Wednesday paper quoted the central bank as saying it would soon raise nominal rates, dealers said.
On money market call money and longer-term rates also rose.
The central bank's chief was quoted by a paper as saying the bank would raise its nominal rates in the next few weeks to offset the effects of the government flood relief credit.
"The zloty rose in early trade on the central bank's statement," said Slawomir Wychowski, a forex dealer at Bank Gospodarki Zywnosciowej SA.

At 0820 GMT the zloty was at -1.08/-1.14 percent from the trading band centre against -1.37/-1.48 at opening. It was at 3.4615/40 against the dollar and 1.8835/50 against the mark versus 3.4680/90 and 1.8880/00 at opening, respectively.
Dealers expected the local unit to firm slightly further.
"The zloty will continue to firm slightly, but the gains should not be higher than 0.1 percent," said Pawel Grajewski, a dealer at Bank Creditanstalt SA in Warsaw.
Dealers said the zloty might stabilise at around one percent below the parity rate and did not expect any NBP interventions on a rising, but low-volume market.

On the money market O/N were at opening levels of around 1.00 percent but T/N and long-term rates grew on the rate rise remarks and the start of the new, August reserve on Thursday. T/N were at 24.2/24.90 percent against 4.00 percent at opening.
Dealers said T/N rates were likely to stay at around 25 percent at offer from Thursday onwards.
"T/N offers at 25 percent will be normal as of tomorrow," said Mariusz Dudek, a dealer at Societe Generale. Currently the central bank's lombard rate is at 25 percent. @
The finance ministry is offering 150 million zlotys of one-year index-linked bonds on Wednesday and 300 million zlotys worth of variable interest three-year bonds.
